findings.title: Date-override zero-length check compares Dayjs objects by reference
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` uses `===` on two freshly constructed Dayjs objects, which is always false. The intended zero-length override check never fires. It should compare with `isSame` or the underlying timestamps.

findings.title: A non-matching override on the same day makes the slot unavailable even when another override covers it
findings.body: `dateOverrides.find` returns true on the first override for the same day that does not contain the slot (e.g. `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)` at line ~123). When a day has several override ranges, e.g. 10-11 and 14-15, a 14:00 slot is rejected because the 10-11 override 'doesn't contain it', even though the 14-15 override does. The check should be 'some override contains the slot', not 'any override on that day fails to contain it'.

findings.title: Date override day matching mixes wall-clock shifting with UTC comparison
findings.body: The override start is shifted by the organizer's UTC offset and then formatted as a date, and the result is compared against `slotStartTime.format(...)`, which is in UTC. Slots near midnight can therefore be matched to the wrong override day, or be treated as having no override and fall through to the other checks. The override and slot must be compared in the same timezone.

findings.title: Working-hours check is inverted for split shifts and ignores timezone
findings.body: `workingHours.find(...)` returns true if the slot falls outside any single working-hours block (`start < startTime || end > endTime`), and then the slot is rejected. With multiple blocks in a day, a slot inside block 2 is outside block 1, so it is rejected. The check should be 'some block contains the slot'. In addition, `slotStartTime` is UTC while `workingHours` are minutes in the organizer timezone, so the comparison is wrong for any non-UTC organizer.

findings.title: Slot end minutes are computed from slotStartTime, so the window is zero-length
findings.body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime.hour()/minute()` instead of `slotEndTime`. The `start` and `end` values are therefore identical, and the `end > workingHour.endTime` condition never tests the slot's actual end. Slots that run past the end of working hours are not rejected.

findings.title: Override timeZone may be undefined and is then interpreted in server local timezone
findings.body: `timeZone: availability.timeZone` is spread into each override, but `timeZone` is optional in `TimeRange`. In slots.ts `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` with undefined falls back to the server's local timezone, which is wrong on the server and makes the override shift depend on where the process runs.

findings.title: Override offset is computed from Date.toString() and only hour/minute of the shifted time is kept
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` re-parses a locale-formatted date string, losing milliseconds and depending on the server's local timezone. The shifted start/end are then reduced to `hour()*60+minute()`, dropping the date. If the timezone shift crosses midnight, the override start/end minutes are wrong (e.g. an override ending at 00:30 after shifting would be treated as 30 minutes after the start rather than the next day).

findings.title: New test does not cover the fixed-host round-robin behaviour the PR fixes
findings.body: The only added test checks that a single-host override yields identical UTC slots in another timezone. Nothing tests the main fix: a round-robin event with a fixed host having a date override should only show slots where the fixed host is available. There is also no test for multiple override ranges on one day or for split working hours, which the new checks break as noted above.
